text:
alex: heads-up — we just got a high-sev support escalation from Acme about p95/p99 spikes on text-gen endpoints. They attached traces showing lots of +200ms tail latency starting ~01:10 UTC. Observed across two shards. Suspect KV/prefix cache thrash

priya: thanks for flagging. any correlation with deployment or config changes?

alex: no deploys in that window. infra metrics show cache_hit_ratio for prefix-cache dropped from ~92% to 48% and evictions spiked. KV miss rate jumped correspondingly. attaching snippet from infra logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T01:09:58Z] prefix_cache.eviction_count=1372 shard=shard-7
[2026-03-15T01:10:04Z] prefix_cache.hit_rate=0.48 shard=shard-7
[2026-03-15T01:10:04Z] kv_store.get_ms.p95=34 p99=220
```

mateo: ugh cache thrash again. any recent traffic pattern changes? big fanout of short prompts?

alex: customer reported a new A/B test that adds dynamic system prompts per request (so more unique prefixes). We think increased cardinality + small cache size per shard caused thrash.

nora: if it's prefix cardinality explosion that fits. the cache is currently a hybrid TTL+LRU with 64k entries per shard. We saw similar in jan but less frequent. Could also be a cache key bug where model+prompt suffix not normalized causing near-unique keys.

priya: can we confirm key distribution? metrics for prefix_key_uniques over last hour?

ben: pulling metrics now — `sum(prefix_cache.unique_keys) by (shard)` shows spike from ~40k to 190k on shard-7 over 10m window.

alex: that matches. also seeing higher variance in sequence lengths which may reduce reuse.

priya: mitigation plan suggestions: 1) quick rollback of the A/B for Acme (customer can revert) 2) increase prefix_cache.entries per shard to 128k temporarily 3) add a cheap normalization step to cache key generation to collapse known dynamic tokens 4) add admission control to avoid caching extremely low-reuse prefixes (e.g., if prefix length < 10 and contains dynamic id)

mateo: agree. for immediate relief, 2 + 3 are fastest. but watch memory usage — shards already at ~70% mem. we can do a staged increase behind FF.

nora: short-term patch: change eviction_policy to 'segmented-lru' to protect frequently-used prefixes from being evicted by high-churn items. we've got code for seg-lru in staging. can we toggle via runtime config?

ben: yes seg-lru is behind flag `prefcache.seg_lru.enabled`. we can flip on shard-7 and 8 to test. also flag for `prefcache.max_entries` adjustable per shard.

alex: repro steps for support / SRE to confirm locally: 
1) run the load generator with a mixture of stable prefixes and high-cardinality dynamic prefixes (script: `tools/loadgen/prefix_thrash.py --stable 1000 --dynamic 50000 --qps 250`)
2) tail the metrics `curl -s http://metrics-host:9100/metrics | grep prefix_cache`
3) confirm hit_rate drop and eviction spike within 5-7 minutes

priya: good. I'll open a rollback ticket with support and ask Acme to disable the A/B while we triage.

mateo: operational steps I'll take in parallel: 
- enable seg-lru on shard-7 and shard-8 behind the FF (deploy config flip)
- bump max_entries from 64k to 96k on those shards (not full 128k yet)
- enable a sampling rate for cache keys to log normalized vs raw keys for 5 minutes (so we can verify normalization coverage)

nora: also recommend adding a new metric `prefix_cache.cardinality_rolling_1m` and an alert if it grows > 2x baseline for a shard. helps catch this earlier.

ben: I'll push a short-term runbook note to PagerDuty playbook: "cache thrash — flip seg-lru + bump entries + check mem; rollback customer AB if no improvement in 10m".

alex: long-term follow-ups (post-mitigation): 
- implement prefix canonicalization layer (strip dynamic tokens, normalize timestamps/IDs) in keygen pipeline
- auto-scaling of cache size based on working set heuristics (not raw unique keys)
- smarter eviction tuned to inter-request reuse patterns (hot prefix pinning)
- integration test that simulates A/B cardinality increases to prevent regressions

priya: also add a per-customer prefix usage quota to protect shared shards from noisy tenants. This could be part of routing policy to route heavy-cardinality customers to dedicated pools.

mateo: flipping seg-lru now on shard-7/8. status: seg-lru=true on shard-7, mem usage +1.4%, prefix_hit_rate back to ~78% after ~6 minutes. Evictions down ~60%. p95 latency improving in traces. :rocket:

alex: great — keep monitoring 10m window. if stable, we can roll to others and keep entries bump only for a few hours then evaluate.

ben: pagerduty note created and emailed Acme contact. oncall-bot: marking incident as "mitigated - cache thrash"

oncall-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated severity=high annotations=[cache-thrash, p99-regression]

nora: follow-up action items assigned: //a) infra to add cardinality metric & alert b) runtime team to ship canonicalization c) product to discuss per-customer routing limits d) support to confirm Acme stability

alex: thanks all. I'll summarize in postmortem draft in #incidents after we close. :thumbsup:
